$comment: Type-check-only configuration for scripts/security/check-edge-functions.mjs.
NOT a deno.json — the name is deliberate. Deno auto-discovers a file called
`deno.json` by walking UP from the entry point, and the entry points are in
supabase/functions/. Nothing must pick this up implicitly: it is passed
explicitly with `deno check --config`, it affects no other Deno invocation in
CI, it affects no deploy, and it changes no source file.
Two entries, both for the same reason: this gate answers ONE question — do
the Edge Functions type-check — and a red that names a different question is
the exact failure mode this suite exists to prevent.
## 1. `imports` — repairing a broken upstream declaration
`@supabase/supabase-js@2.55.0` ships this line in its own type declarations
(dist/module/lib/types.d.ts:4):
import { StorageClientOptions } from '@supabase/storage-js/dist/module/StorageClient'
a deep import into a subpath of a dependency it pins only as a RANGE,
`^2.10.4`. storage-js has since been restructured to a flat bundle: 2.99.3
ships dist/index.d.mts and dist/index.d.cts and no dist/module/ directory at
all. The subpath that declaration reaches for does not exist in the version
the range resolves to.
esm.sh resolves that range when it builds, rewrites the specifier to
https://esm.sh/@supabase/storage-js@2.99.3/dist/module/StorageClient, and then
its build service HANGS on the missing file rather than returning 404 — every
request answers `408 Request Timeout` after ~30s, indefinitely.
`deno check` follows x-typescript-types, so the gate died — on all 184 entry
points importing supabase-js@2.55.0 — the moment esm.sh re-resolved that
range. It looked exactly like a registry outage and is not one: no amount of
retrying, caching or waiting resolves a subpath that does not exist. Two
commits were spent shortening the window on a blip this never was.
This is not a weakening. The right-hand side is the SAME PACKAGE at the SAME
VERSION — 2.99.3's real declarations, which do declare StorageClientOptions
(index.d.mts:2676) and do export it (:2735). It repairs a specifier upstream
got wrong; it does not stub a type, silence a diagnostic or relax a check.
Every other specifier resolves exactly as before, and check-edge-functions.mjs
still refuses to report a number when resolution fails — so a NEW broken
import still fails the gate rather than hiding behind this one.
Delete it when nothing imports a supabase-js whose types reach into
storage-js's dist/module/ — because esm.sh serves that path, because the
pinned supabase-js versions move to a release that no longer deep-imports it,
or because these functions move to `npm:` specifiers, which resolve types
from the tarball and never involve esm.sh's build service at all.
## 2. `minimumDependencyAge` — a real control, at the wrong control point
Deno 2.9 refuses an npm package published within the last 24 hours:
Could not find npm package '@lovable.dev/mcp-js' matching '0.26.2'.
A newer matching version was found, but it was not used because it was
newer than the specified minimum dependency date of 2026-08-10 ...
That is a good default and this is the wrong place to enforce it.
supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts is GENERATED by a Lovable sync, which pins
the version it has just published — so the pin is always fresh, and the gate
would be red for a day after every sync, naming a supply-chain concern while
the type errors it exists to catch went unreported.
Decisive: the same sync deploys that dependency to production, and no deploy
path applies an age policy. Blocking the type-check does not delay the
dependency by one second — it delays only the type-check. The risk has
already been taken by the time this gate runs.
Dependency risk is owned elsewhere and still is: the `supply-chain` job
(npm audit, scripts/security/dependency-audit.mjs), Dependabot, GitGuardian
and gitleaks. This flag is scoped to one `deno check` invocation and does not
touch any of them.
